subject: Cross-zone co-term consolidation and surge policy for Horizon Labs
messages:
From: Alyssa Chen <alyssa@horizon-labs.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.ai>, Camila Reyes <camila@redwood.ai>
Cc: procurement@horizon-labs.com
Date: Tue, 12 May 2026 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: Cross-zone co-term consolidation and surge policy

Hi Jonas / Camila,

Thanks for the quick catch-up last week. Horizon is approaching our renewal window (current term ends 2026-08-31) and we have two related asks we'd like Redwood to help structure:

1) Aligning multiple accounts/regions onto a single co-term (we run separate clusters for NA and EU and want a consolidated commercial term)
2) A formal surge policy: predictable credits for short-term capacity spikes (we expect a 20-30% quarterly variance)

High-level preferences: multi-year (2 year) with optional ramping (year 1 at 70% committed, year 2 at 120% of year 1), co-terming across zones, and an auto-renew clause with 60d notice opt-out. We are open to an annual true-up.

Attached: Horizon_Renewal_Request_v1.pdf (summary + expected capacity growth)

Can you share 2–3 structure options and a rough unit economics delta (tokens per $1k) for each? Procurement would like a short list to decide which to move to legal.

Best,
Alyssa
Director, Cloud Platforms
Horizon Labs

---
From: Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.ai>
To: Alyssa Chen <alyssa@horizon-labs.com>
Cc: Camila Reyes <camila@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 13 May 2026 10:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Cross-zone co-term consolidation and surge policy

Alyssa — thanks for the clear ask and the attachment. Putting a short set of practical options below to take to procurement/legal. Copying pricing & renewals to confirm feasibility.

Option A — Sync & Commit (lowest unit price)- 24 month co-term across NA + EU, fixed committed tokens per region aggregated to a single committed pool.- Year 1 commit = 70% of current run rate; Year 2 = 120% of Year 1 commit.- Annual true-up + 30% surge buffer (charged at lower burst rate); auto-renew unless 60d notice.

Option B — Staged Co-term with Surge Credits (preferred middle ground)- 24 month co-term; staged committed increases at quarter boundaries (quarterly ramp schedule).- Surge credit pool: 10% of committed tokens reserved for bursts (applied as credits against billed overages).- Auto-renew but with an annual price-review band (±5%).

Option C — Flex-Reserve (more operational flexibility)- 12 month base term with optional 12 month extension that auto-activates if aggregate consumption >110% of committed in Q4.- Surge pricing on-demand; no pre-allocated credits.

I attached a quick delta worksheet (RW_proposal_options_20260513.xlsx) with example unit economics and sample invoices. Quick note: because of multi-region routing and dedicated pools, a consolidated co-term reduces per-token overhead by ~8–12% vs two independent contracts. Marissa/Karthik — can you confirm which of these we can support without custom SLA changes? Also, any billing cadence implications for co-terming across regions?

Thanks — happy to jump on a 30 min call tomorrow to walk procurement through options.

Jonas
Sr. Account Executive | Redwood Inference

Folks — quick pricing/legal note after reviewing:

1) We can support Option B as the default commercial for Horizon. Surge credits (10% pool) are simple to implement and map cleanly in billing as a credit ledger entry — no SLA changes required.

2) Auto-renew with 60d notice is acceptable; legal asks for a mutual right-to-terminate on material breach and an annual CPI-linked price band (±5%) to be explicit in contract language.

3) For co-terming across regions: billing will be consolidated but we need to call out data residency boundaries and routing policies in the Statement of Work. That will be an operational attachment — no change to core terms but we must include an "aggregation rider".

4) Action: I recommend we send Option B as the baseline and include a short addendum that spells out the ramp schedule and true-up cadence. If Horizon accepts, we push to a 2-page commercial memo + DocuSign.

I'll draft commercial language and a short redline for legal. Jonas — if you want me to include the optional 12-month fallback (Option C) as a schedule, I can add it.

Marissa Cole
